title: An Instagram Influencer Just Outranked Shah Rukh Khan on IMDb. Maa Behen Is Netflix's Wildest Indian Hit.
excerpt: Dharna Durga — content creator, Netflix debutante, and now India's fifth most popular celebrity on IMDb — has left Madhuri Dixit and Triptii Dimri in the dust. Welcome to the new Bollywood.
body:
Here's a sentence nobody predicted writing in 2026: an Instagram influencer making her film debut just outranked Shah Rukh Khan, Madhuri Dixit, and Triptii Dimri on IMDb's most popular Indian celebrities list. And she did it in her first week.

Dharna Durga — 26, massive social following, zero film credits before last Wednesday — shot to the fifth spot on IMDb's popular Indian celebrities ranking after Maa Behen dropped on Netflix on June 4. Her co-star Triptii Dimri, fresh off a monster year, landed at 13th. Madhuri Dixit, a living legend, came in at 15th. The paparazzi at the premiere barely looked at Dharna. The internet had other plans.

The Film That Came for Everyone

Maa Behen is a black comedy thriller directed by Suresh Triveni — the man behind Jalsa and Tumhari Sulu, a filmmaker who knows exactly how to make middle-class chaos feel cinematic. The premise is deceptively simple: Rekha, a loud, unapologetic single mother living in a conservative colony, calls her grown-up daughters home after a neighbour dies. What follows is a spiralling, dark, hilarious unravelling of family secrets, patriarchal expectations, and the particular kind of violence that happens behind closed doors with a smile.

Madhuri Dixit as Rekha is having the time of her life. She hasn't been this loose and unpredictable on screen in years — part matriarch, part provocateur, every inch the star who earned her throne. Triptii Dimri brings a coiled, reactive energy as one of the daughters, constantly torn between loyalty and horror. But it's Dharna who lands the surprise punches. Her timing is impeccable, her line readings feel unscripted (in the best way), and she carries a naturalism that trained actors sometimes spend years chasing.

"Being a part of Maa Behen has been an unforgettable experience. The film embraces imperfection, family chaos, and all the unexpected twists that life throws at us." — Dharna Durga

Netflix's Global Win

The numbers tell the story. Maa Behen hit #2 on Netflix's Global Top 10 Non-English Films within its first week — sitting just below a Korean thriller, outpacing everything from Latin America, Europe, and the rest of Asia. For an Indian film that isn't a war epic, a period drama, or a franchise sequel, that's a seismic result. This is a black comedy about a mother and her daughters in a small-town colony. And the world is watching.

Produced by Abundantia Entertainment in association with Opening Image Films, the film also features strong work from Ravi Kishan, Geetanjali Kulkarni, Arunoday Singh, and Shardul Bhardwaj — a supporting cast that turns every dinner table scene into a pressure cooker.

What Dharna's Rise Actually Means

The IMDb ranking isn't just trivia. It's based on page visits — real people searching for a name they saw on screen and wanting to know more. That means millions of Netflix viewers across the globe watched Maa Behen, saw Dharna Durga, and immediately went looking for her. Not Madhuri. Not Triptii. Her.

This is what the new Bollywood pipeline looks like. You build an audience on Instagram, you get cast in a Netflix original directed by one of Bollywood's sharpest filmmakers, and you blow up globally in six days. No film-family lineage required. No decade of struggling through auditions. Just talent meeting platform at the exact right moment.

The old guard isn't being replaced — Madhuri is extraordinary in this film. But the door is wider now, and Dharna Durga just kicked it open.

Maa Behen is streaming now on Netflix worldwide.
